# [CS036] Unbounded HTTP Request Body Read (http-unbounded-body-read)

A request body is read completely without a size limit.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-400](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html) |
| **OWASP** | A06:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

io.ReadAll(r.Body) and decoders on r.Body read whatever the client sends, so one large request can exhaust memory. http.MaxBytesReader and io.LimitReader bound the read.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
body, err := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
body, err := io.ReadAll(http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, 1<<20))
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [http-unbounded-body-read]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    http-unbounded-body-read: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore http-unbounded-body-read -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** http-unbounded-body-read
```
